candidates.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat

distinctFrom.why: implement family differs (kettlebell vs dumbbell); kettlebell horn grip changes hand/forearm position and keeps the bell closer to the sternum than a dumbbell held vertically

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (kettlebell/ballistic training chapter)
candidates.notes: Standard KB squat entry point; front-loaded hold makes an upright torso self-correcting.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Front Rack Squat (Single-Arm)

distinctFrom.why: unilateral offset rack load adds a resisted anti-lateral-flexion demand the two-hand goblet hold does not

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Offset load in one rack position; core resists lateral lean, so it is not just a one-arm goblet squat.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Front Rack Squat (Double)

distinctFrom.why: laterality differs (bilateral, two implements); load is symmetric so no anti-lateral-flexion demand

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Two kettlebells racked at the shoulders; the standard heavier progression from goblet squat once bell size outgrows a comfortable goblet hold.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Overhead Squat

distinctFrom.why: load held locked out overhead rather than racked; adds sustained overhead shoulder-stability demand through the full squat

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Rarely programmed for volume; used as a stability/mobility skill piece more than a hypertrophy squat.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Deadlift

distinctFrom.why: starts and resets from the floor each rep (full ROM pick-up) rather than a standing hip hinge that never returns the bell to the floor

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (kettlebell/ballistic training chapter)
candidates.notes: The floor-to-lockout pull the swing and clean both begin from; a common first hinge pattern taught before ballistics.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift

distinctFrom.why: wide stance and vertical shin shift emphasis toward adductors/glutes and shorten the pulling range versus the close-stance version

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: No existing glute subregion matches hip_extension exactly (glute subregions in the seed are activator/pumper/stretcher); left null rather than guessed.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Single-Leg Deadlift

distinctFrom.why: laterality differs (unilateral stance); adds a balance/hip-stability demand a bilateral pull does not have

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Free hand typically counterbalances; balance demand is the main coaching variable, not load.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Swing (Single-Arm)

distinctFrom.why: unilateral loading adds an anti-rotation demand through the hips and trunk the two-hand version does not carry

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated per EL-5.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Swing (Alternating)

distinctFrom.why: laterality differs (alternating hand switch mid-flight adds a timing/grip-transfer skill the single-arm version does not require)

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated. Hand switch at the top of the arc is the coached skill point.

candidates.name: Double Kettlebell Swing

distinctFrom.why: two implements held simultaneously; wider stance and grip spacing change the swing arc versus one bell held with both hands

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated. Requires two matched bells, which limits how often gyms can offer it (niche over specialist).

candidates.name: Kettlebell Clean

distinctFrom.why: racks the bell and stops there; no overhead press phase, so it trains the pull-and-catch skill in isolation

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated. The standalone building block the corpus’s combined clean-and-press skips.

candidates.name: Double Kettlebell Clean

distinctFrom.why: laterality differs (two bells cleaned together); the bells must be threaded past the thighs simultaneously, a distinct technical demand

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Dead Clean

distinctFrom.why: each rep resets dead on the floor with no backswing, removing the stretch-reflex momentum the standard clean uses

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Ballistic (still an explosive hip-driven pull) even though it starts dead; never auto-generated. Common strict-technique regression for clean coaching.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Hang Clean

distinctFrom.why: starts from a hang position above the knee rather than the floor, shortening the pull and removing the floor pick-up phase

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated.

candidates.name: Alternating Kettlebell Snatch

distinctFrom.why: laterality differs (alternating hand switch at the top, mid-arc), the standard competition/conditioning format

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Press (Single-Arm)

distinctFrom.why: strict press from the rack only; no clean phase, so it isolates the press for its own progression

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: The strict overhead press most KB strength programmes actually track, separate from the combined clean-and-press skill.

candidates.name: Double Kettlebell Press

distinctFrom.why: laterality differs (bilateral, two implements pressed together); removes the anti-lateral-flexion demand of the single-arm version

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Requires two matched bells.

candidates.name: Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Press

distinctFrom.why: bell held base-up, unsupported by the forearm; the wrist/grip must actively balance it through the whole press

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Grip-stability drill more than a loading tool; light weights only by design, so it stays niche rather than specialist.

candidates.name: Half-Kneeling Kettlebell Press

distinctFrom.why: kneeling stance removes leg drive and adds an anti-rotation demand through the hips, isolating the shoulder press more strictly

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Common shoulder-stability accessory; kneeling limb is opposite the pressing arm by convention.

candidates.name: Seated Kettlebell Press

distinctFrom.why: seated position removes leg drive and torso lean entirely, isolating the shoulder more than the standing version

sources: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (kettlebell/ballistic training chapter)
candidates.notes: Named seated per the corpus’s standing-is-default naming convention. axialLoad true matches the corpus convention for seated FREE-WEIGHT presses (e.g. "Seated Dumbbell Press"): no fixed backrest transmits the load to a frame, so the spine still bears it, unlike a seated machine press.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Floor Press

distinctFrom.why: lying on the floor, horizontal press pattern (chest-dominant) rather than a standing vertical/overhead press

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Floor limits ROM at the bottom, taking the shoulder joint out of end-range; a common alternative when no bench is available.

candidates.name: See-Saw Kettlebell Press

distinctFrom.why: the two bells press in reciprocating fashion (one up as the other lowers) rather than together, adding a coordination and anti-rotation demand

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Requires two matched bells; coordination-focused rather than a primary loading tool.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Push Press

distinctFrom.why: uses a leg-drive dip and drive to launch the bell, so heavier loads move than a strict press; the leg contribution is the defining difference

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (kettlebell/ballistic training chapter)
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated per EL-5 (explicit brief instruction).

candidates.name: Kettlebell Jerk

distinctFrom.why: adds a second dip under the bell to catch the lockout (split or re-bend of the knees), rather than one continuous leg drive to lockout

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated per EL-5 (explicit brief instruction). Competition girevoy-sport lift.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Row (Single-Arm)

distinctFrom.why: new movement family for this corpus: no existing kettlebell row row exists (only the swing/snatch/clean/press/RDL/shrug/get-up rows are seeded)

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (kettlebell/ballistic training chapter)
candidates.notes: Bent-over or supported single-arm row; a direct kettlebell-equipment equivalent of the existing Dumbbell Row.

candidates.name: Gorilla Row

distinctFrom.why: both bells stay on the floor between the feet and the lifter rows alternately from a fixed deep-hinge stance, adding a static hip-hinge hold the supported single-arm row does not have

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Two kettlebells on the floor, deep athletic stance held throughout.

candidates.name: Renegade Row

distinctFrom.why: performed from a push-up plank position (hands on the bells) rather than a standing hinge, adding a whole-body anti-rotation plank demand

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: High core and shoulder-stability demand; light loads relative to the standing row variants.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Farmer's Carry

distinctFrom.why: implement family differs (kettlebell vs dumbbell); the bell’s handle geometry sits differently in the hand than a dumbbell head

sources: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (kettlebell/ballistic training chapter)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps (carries convention); rep fields left null.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Suitcase Carry

distinctFrom.why: implement family differs (kettlebell vs dumbbell)

sources: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (kettlebell/ballistic training chapter)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Rack Carry

distinctFrom.why: bell held racked at the shoulder rather than hanging at the side; the anti-lateral-flexion demand moves from the hip/oblique line to the upper trunk and shoulder girdle

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Overhead Carry

distinctFrom.why: bell locked out overhead rather than racked; sustained overhead shoulder stability replaces the rack-position anti-flexion demand

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps.

candidates.name: Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Carry

distinctFrom.why: bell held base-up unsupported through the whole walk; grip and wrist must actively balance it, unlike a racked bell resting on the forearm

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps. Light-load stability drill; stays niche given the load ceiling.

candidates.name: Mixed Kettlebell Carry

distinctFrom.why: one bell racked and one suitcase-carried simultaneously; the asymmetric combination changes the anti-rotation/anti-lateral-flexion mix versus either carry alone

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps.

candidates.name: Turkish Get-Up (Half)

distinctFrom.why: stops at the tall-sitting/half-kneeling midpoint and returns, rather than completing the full stand-to-lying sequence; a regression used to teach the pattern

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Coaching progression toward the full get-up; overheadPosition true because the bell is kept locked out overhead throughout, same as the full get-up.

candidates.name: Get-Up to Elbow

distinctFrom.why: stops even earlier, at the roll-to-forearm/elbow phase; the most reduced segment of the get-up sequence

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: The earliest get-up progression segment; often the first drill taught before any weight is used overhead, so the bell is not locked overhead the way the fuller get-up variants are.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Windmill (Low)

distinctFrom.why: new movement family for this corpus: no existing windmill row is seeded

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Bell racked at the shoulder (not locked overhead) throughout the hip hinge; the mobility/strength hybrid entry version.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Windmill (High)

distinctFrom.why: bell stays locked out overhead throughout the hinge instead of racked, adding a sustained overhead shoulder-stability demand to the hip mobility work

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Advanced shoulder-stability/mobility skill; rarely loaded heavily.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Halo

distinctFrom.why: new movement family for this corpus: circles the bell around the head, a shoulder-mobility pattern none of the seeded kettlebell rows perform

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Light-load mobility/warm-up staple in kettlebell programming; rarely a primary volume driver.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Around-the-World

distinctFrom.why: passes the bell around the waist hand-to-hand rather than around the head; a torso-level pass instead of a shoulder-level circle

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Grip-transfer/coordination drill; almost never logged as working volume, so niche rather than specialist.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Reverse Lunge (Rack Position)

distinctFrom.why: new movement family for this corpus: no existing kettlebell lunge row is seeded

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: One or two bells racked; stepping back is generally lower knee-shear than stepping forward, the common default teaching cue.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Forward Lunge (Rack Position)

distinctFrom.why: stepping direction reverses (forward instead of back), which changes the deceleration demand on the front leg on landing

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Higher knee-shear on the step; programmed less often than the reverse-step version.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Overhead Lunge

distinctFrom.why: bell held locked out overhead instead of racked, adding a sustained overhead shoulder-stability demand through the step and stand

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
candidates.notes: Advanced combination skill; light loads only.

candidates.name: Kettlebell Thruster (Double)

distinctFrom.why: the squat continues into a full overhead press at the top of each rep rather than stopping at standing

sources: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (kettlebell/ballistic training chapter)
candidates.notes: Not classified ballistic under EL-7 (the ballistic list is swing/clean/snatch/jerk/throw/jump); this is a continuous squat-to-press, not a launch.

candidates.name: Kettlebell High Pull

distinctFrom.why: the hip-drive momentum is pulled into a high elbow finish at chest height rather than let float out to arm’s length

sources: StrongFirst (Tsatsouline, "Kettlebell Simple & Sinister"; StrongFirst Kettlebell instructor manual)
RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never auto-generated per EL-5 (explicit brief instruction: every high pull is never_auto).

candidates.name: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift High Pull

distinctFrom.why: starts from a sumo-stance deadlift pick-up with the bell between the feet rather than a swing-style backswing start

sources: RKC/Dragon Door Kettlebell instructor curriculum
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (kettlebell/ballistic training chapter)
candidates.notes: Ballistic; never_auto per the brief’s explicit call-out (this specific named movement is flagged separately from the general high-pull rule, since the combined internal-rotation-plus-abduction shoulder position at the top is coached with more caution than a plain high pull).

rejected.name: Kettlebell Figure 8
rejected.reason: not distinct under EL-2 (a coordination/flow drill built from the halo and around-the-world patterns already covered; no single coach-countable stimulus of its own)

rejected.name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Clean
rejected.reason: not distinct under EL-2 (the bottoms-up demand is already represented by Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Press and Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Carry; a bottoms-up clean is a rare combination drill, not a distinct stimulus a coach would separately track)

rejected.name: Kettlebell Snatch Test
rejected.reason: not representable (a timed-rep-count test protocol, not a single exercise row)

rejected.name: Long Cycle Clean and Jerk
rejected.reason: not distinct under EL-2 (rep-scheme label for repeated Kettlebell Clean + Kettlebell Jerk, not a new movement)
